whitePlan: Claim the center with a pawn, so your pieces have room to come out.

white.name: King's Pawn Opening
white.idea: Your e-pawn grabs the center. It also opens lines for your queen and your light-squared bishop.

children.idea: Black pushes the e-pawn two squares and claims the center too.
children.plan: Get a knight out so it attacks their pawn on e5.

children.idea: Your knight jumps toward the center and attacks the pawn on e5. Knights are strongest near the middle of the board.
Black's knight comes out and defends the pawn on e5.
children.plan: Get your light-squared bishop out where it aims at the weak pawn next to their king.

children.name: Italian Game
children.idea: Your bishop on c4 aims at f7, a square only Black's king protects. Next, get your king safe.

children.name: Giuoco Piano
children.idea: Black's bishop comes out and aims at f2, the weak square next to your king.
children.plan: Get ready to build a bigger center with your pawns, or get your king safe first.

children.idea: Your pawn on c3 gets ready to make your center bigger. It also takes the d4 square away from Black's knight.
Black's knight comes out and attacks your pawn on e4.
children.plan: Keep your pawn on e4 protected, then get your king safe.

children.idea: Your pawn on d3 protects e4 and opens a path for your dark-squared bishop. Next, get your king safe.
Your king is tucked into the corner and your rook is closer to the center. Next, build a solid center with your pawns.
Black's knight comes out and attacks your pawn on e4.
children.plan: Keep your pawn on e4 protected, and keep building a solid center.

children.idea: Your pawn on d3 guards e4 and frees your bishop on c1. Next, make your center stronger and get your last knight out.

children.name: Two Knights Defense
children.idea: Black's knight comes out and attacks your pawn on e4 instead of copying your bishop.
children.plan: Keep it simple: protect your pawn on e4 calmly, then get your king safe.

children.idea: Your pawn on d3 guards e4 and opens the way for your bishop on c1. Next, get your king safe and get your other knight out.
Black's bishop comes out and aims at f2, the weak square next to your king.
children.plan: Get your king safe now.

children.idea: Your king is safe in the corner and your rook can join the game.
Black's bishop comes out quietly and stays close to the king.
children.plan: Get your king safe, then keep bringing out your pieces.

children.idea: Your king is safe and your rook is ready to join the game. Next, get your other knight out without blocking your c-pawn.
Black guards e5 with a pawn but hems in the bishop on f8, which can now only go to e7.
children.plan: Get your king safe, then use your pawns to take more of the center.

children.name: Hungarian Defense
children.idea: Black's bishop comes out very safely and stays close to the king.
children.plan: Grab more of the center with a pawn, or stay calm and get your king safe.

children.name: Philidor Defense
children.idea: Black defends e5 with a pawn, but that blocks in the bishop on f8.
children.plan: Take more of the center with a pawn, and get your pieces out quickly.

children.name: Petrov Defense
children.idea: Black's knight attacks your pawn on e4 instead of defending the pawn on e5.
children.plan: Protect your pawn on e4 and get a new piece out at the same time.

children.name: Sicilian Defense
children.idea: Black pushes a side pawn that fights for the middle of the board.
children.plan: Get a knight out, then get ready to open the center with a pawn.

children.name: French Defense
children.idea: Black gets ready to attack your pawn on e4 with the d-pawn next.
children.plan: Make your center bigger with a second pawn beside the one you have.

children.name: Scandinavian Defense
children.idea: Black's pawn attacks your pawn on e4 right away.
children.plan: Deal with the attack on your pawn. If their queen comes out early, chase it while you get your pieces out.

black.name: King's Pawn Opening
black.idea: White pushes the e-pawn two squares and grabs the center.
black.plan: Claim your share of the center with a pawn.

children.idea: Your pawn on e5 claims the center and opens lines for your queen and your dark-squared bishop. Next, bring out your knights.
White's knight comes out and attacks your pawn on e5.
children.plan: Protect your pawn on e5 and get a piece out at the same time.

children.idea: Your knight on c6 protects e5 and develops toward the center. It also watches the d4 square.

children.name: Italian Game
children.idea: White's bishop aims at f7, the weak square next to your king.
children.plan: Get your bishop out too, so it aims at the weak square next to their king.

children.name: Giuoco Piano
children.idea: Your bishop on c5 aims at f2, White's weak spot. Next, get a knight out and get your king safe.
White gets ready to grab more of the center and chase your bishop.
children.plan: Get a knight out so it attacks their pawn on e4.

children.idea: Your knight attacks the pawn on e4 and clears the way for your king to get safe. If White attacks one of your pawns, look at every way to answer.
White's king tucks into the corner, where it is safe.
children.plan: Get a knight out, then get your own king safe too.

children.idea: Your knight develops and attacks the pawn on e4. Next, get your own king safe too.
White's pawn on d3 now protects the pawn on e4.
children.plan: Get a knight out, then get your king safe.

children.idea: Your knight comes out toward the center. Next, get your king safe.

children.name: Ruy Lopez
children.idea: White's bishop attacks your knight on c6, the piece guarding e5.
children.plan: Chase the bishop with a pawn so it has to step back or trade.

children.idea: Your pawn on a6 attacks the bishop, so it has to step back or trade itself for your knight.
The bishop steps back but still looks at your knight on c6.
children.plan: Get a knight out so it attacks their pawn on e4.

children.idea: Your knight develops and attacks the pawn on e4. Next, get your dark-squared bishop out and get your king safe.
White's bishop trades itself for your knight.
children.plan: Win your piece back, and pick the capture that opens lines for your queen and your light-squared bishop.

children.idea: Your queen and your bishop on c8 now have open lines. If White's knight grabs your pawn on e5, look for a queen attack on two things at once.

children.name: Scotch Game
children.idea: White pushes the d-pawn and opens the center right away.
children.plan: Their pawn now attacks your pawn on e5. Look at every way to answer that attack, and pick one that keeps your pieces coming out fast.

children.idea: You win a pawn, and White will usually win it back with the knight. Then get your pieces out quickly.
White's knight wins the pawn back and now sits in the center.
children.plan: Get a knight out so it attacks their pawn on e4.

children.idea: Your knight develops and attacks the pawn on e4. Next, get a bishop out and get your king safe.

children.name: Vienna Game
children.idea: White's knight comes out and protects the pawn on e4.
children.plan: Get a knight out toward the center, then a bishop, then get your king safe.

children.name: Bishop's Opening
children.idea: White's bishop comes out early and aims at f7, the weak square next to your king.
children.plan: Get a knight out so it attacks their pawn on e4, and keep an eye on the weak square next to your king.

children.name: King's Gambit
children.idea: White offers a pawn to open lines toward your king.
children.plan: Is their pawn safe to take? Either way, get your pieces out quickly and keep your king safe.

black.name: Queen's Pawn Opening
black.idea: White pushes the d-pawn two squares and grabs the center.
black.plan: Claim your share of the center with a pawn, so they cannot take it all.

children.idea: Your pawn on d5 stands up to White's pawn on d4. It also opens a path for your light-squared bishop.

children.name: Queen's Gambit
children.idea: White offers the c-pawn to pull your pawn on d5 away from the center.
children.plan: Support your pawn on d5 with another pawn so your center stays strong.

children.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
children.idea: Your pawn on e6 supports d5, so your center stays strong. It also opens the path for your bishop on f8.
White's knight comes out and adds pressure on your pawn on d5.
children.plan: Get a knight out that also guards your pawn on d5.

children.idea: Your knight guards d5 and helps clear the way for your king. Next, get your dark-squared bishop out so your king can get safe.
White's bishop pins your knight on f6 to your queen on d8.
children.plan: Break the pin, then get your king safe.

children.idea: Your bishop on e7 blocks the pin, so your knight on f6 is no longer pinned. Next, get your king safe.
White brings out another knight.
children.plan: Get your dark-squared bishop out so your king can get safe soon.

children.idea: Your bishop on e7 is out and no longer in your king's way. Next, get your king safe.
White's c-pawn captures your d5 pawn.
children.plan: Win the pawn back in the way that keeps a pawn in the center.

children.idea: Your pawn on d5 still holds the center, and your bishop on c8 now has an open path. Next, get your dark-squared bishop out and your king safe.
White's knight comes out toward the center.
children.plan: Get a knight out that also guards your pawn on d5.

children.idea: Your knight guards d5 and helps clear the way for your king. Next, get your dark-squared bishop out so your king can get safe.
White's knight comes out first, before any more pawn pushes.
children.plan: Get your own knight out toward the center.

children.idea: Your knight comes out toward the center and helps guard d5. Next, keep your center strong, then get your bishops out and your king safe.
White's c-pawn attacks your pawn on d5.
children.plan: Support your pawn on d5 with another pawn so your center stays strong.

children.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
children.idea: Your pawn on e6 supports d5, so your center stays strong. It also opens the path for your bishop on f8.

children.name: London System
children.idea: White brings the dark-squared bishop out early.
children.plan: Stay calm and solid: get a knight out toward the center.

children.idea: Your knight develops and helps guard d5. Next, keep your center strong and get your pieces out.
White builds a solid pawn chain.
children.plan: Support your pawn on d5 with another pawn, and open a path for your dark-squared bishop.

children.idea: Your pawns on d5 and e6 form a strong wall. Next, get your bishop out, get your king safe, and later use a pawn to challenge White's center.
